question: Which LLTO coating retained the most capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5C, how does it compare with the pristine NCM, and why did the 2 mol.% coating lower the rate capability?

rendered: The LLTO coating that retained the most capacity was LLTO-2, at 86.2%[1] retention, against 56.6%[2] for the pristine NCM. Both were measured in the same cycling test, cycled at 0.5C[3], over the same cycle count. The other coatings were LLTO-0.5 at 85.5%[4] and LLTO-1 at 57.2%[5], so LLTO-2 leads the set and every LLTO coating beat the pristine NCM except LLTO-1, which was only marginally above it. The paper's stated reason for the lower rate capability at the higher coating loading is given as a possible cause: However, with 2 mol.% coating, the rate capability decreased, which may be due to the increase in the thickness of the coating layer, resulting in the suppression of electron transfer process during charge/discharge cycling.[6] In short, a thicker coating layer is thought to hinder electron transfer during charge and discharge, so rate capability dropped even though the coating improved cycling.
